Which country is Sukhoi Su-17 from?
Sukhoi Su-17: Soviet Union. The Sukhoi Su-17 (Russian: Су-17; NATO reporting name: Fitter) is a variable-sweep wing fighter-bomber developed for the Soviet military.
Who is credited with discovering Pavo?
Pavo (constellation): Petrus Plancius. Pavo is a constellation in the southern sky whose name is Latin for 'peacock'.
Who is credited with discovering Nitroglycerin?
Nitroglycerin: Ascanio Sobrero. It is combined with nitrocellulose to form double-based smokeless powder, used as a propellant in artillery and firearms since the 1880s.
Who is credited with discovering Lithium?
Lithium: Johan August Arfwedson. Lithium (from Ancient Greek: λίθος, líthos, 'stone') is a chemical element; it has symbol Li and atomic number 3.

The only living member of its entire taxonomic order, this nocturnal African mammal digs into termite and ant hills using sharp claws and powerful legs — related distantly to elephants and manatees, what is it?
Aardvark (Orycteropus afer) is a medium-sized, burrowing, nocturnal mammal native to Africa.

This Austrian psychotherapist founded a school of psychology emphasizing birth order and belonging, breaking from Freud by proposing that contributing to others is key to a person's sense of worth — who is he?
Alfred Adler (Austrian; February 7, 1870 - May 28, 1937) was an Austrian medical doctor, psychotherapist, and founder of the school of individual psychology.
Its scientific name translates roughly to 'fused lizard,' and it may be the largest of its armored kind at up to 8 tons — which dinosaur genus?
Ankylosaurus is a genus of armored dinosaur. It was named by Barnum Brown in 1908; it is monotypic, containing only A. magniventris.

Explicitly describing the relativity of motion and, by his own account, 23 years old in 499 CE, this figure is considered the first of the great mathematician-astronomers of classical Indian science — who is he?
Aryabhata (476-550 CE) was the first of the major mathematician-astronomers and early physicist from the classical age of Indian mathematics and Indian astronomy.

Ranking among the largest wild cats, this population of the Panthera tigris tigris subspecies has roamed the Indian subcontinent since the Late Pleistocene and is found from India to southwestern China — name it?
Bengal tiger is a population of the Panthera tigris tigris subspecies. It is distributed from India, southern Nepal, Bangladesh, Bhutan to Southwestern China.
Belonging to the Colubridae family of venomous snakes and found only in Sub-Saharan Africa, this reptile's scientific name is Dispholidus typus — what is it commonly called?
Boomslang (or; Dispholidus typus) is a highly venomous snake in the family Colubridae.
Its three-dimensional shape mimics adenosine closely enough to plug into the same receptors, blocking the brain's signal to wind down — which psychoactive substance is it?
Caffeine is a central nervous system (CNS) stimulant of the methylxanthine class and is the most commonly consumed psychoactive substance globally.
Mature females are cows, the intact males are bulls, and the castrated males pull plows as oxen — all names for one widespread domesticated bovine kept as livestock. What animal is it?
Cattle (Bos taurus) are large, domesticated, bovid ungulates widely kept as livestock.
Grown for blue-flowered roadside roots that become a coffee substitute, or for bitter salad leaves like escarole and radicchio, which plant genus covers both chicory and endive?
Cichorium is a genus of plants in the tribe Cichorieae within the family Asteraceae.

Often called the most renowned Greek mathematician since antiquity, he spent his career in Germany advancing measure theory and the calculus of variations — and even built an axiomatic formulation of thermodynamics. Who was he?
Constantin Carathéodory (13 September 1873 - 2 February 1950) was a Greek mathematician who spent most of his professional career in Germany.
Nearly every genus in this taxonomic family of armadillos is extinct, except for one genus that still includes eight living species today. Name the family?
Dasypodidae is a family of mostly extinct genera of armadillos.
Found in nighttime cold remedies like NyQuil and paired with vitamin B6 for pregnancy-related nausea, this antihistamine is an inverse agonist at the H1 receptor — which drug?
Doxylamine is an antihistamine medication used to treat insomnia and allergies, and - in combination with pyridoxine (vitamin B6) - to treat morning sickness in pregnant women.

These ductless glands throughout the body secrete their products directly into the bloodstream rather than through a duct — together with the pineal, pituitary, thyroid, and others, what are they called?
Endocrine gland is a network of glands and organs located throughout the body.
What is the scientific term for the solid waste material left after digestion, discharged through the anus, and sometimes reused as fertilizer, fuel, or building material?
Feces (also faeces or fces or poop) are the solid or semi-solid remains of food that was not digested in the small intestine, and has been broken down by bacteria in the large intestine.
Named after a German militant group in a reader's 1994 letter and formalized by a Stanford linguist in 2005, this cognitive bias makes newly learned facts seem suddenly everywhere — what is it?

Frequency illusion (also known as the Baader-Meinhof phenomenon or Red Car Theory) is a cognitive bias in which a person notices a specific concept, word, or product more frequently after recently becoming aware of it.

Colorless, odorless, and oddly sweet, this viscous sugar alcohol carries three hydroxyl groups, forms the backbone of every triglyceride in animal fat, and moonlights as a food sweetener — what is it?
Glycerol is a sugar alcohol with chemical formula C3H5(OH)3.
Though usually grouped with the birch family, some botanists split this deciduous shrub genus into its own family — and its nut is a popular snack — which plant?
Hazel are plants of the genus Corylus of deciduous trees and large shrubs native to the temperate Northern Hemisphere.
Named for a Greek youth beloved by Apollo and slain by a jealous wind god who then transformed him into this fragrant spring bloom — what flower genus is it?
Hyacinth is a genus of bulbous herbs and spring-blooming perennials.
Resembling a lump of burnt charcoal growing on birch bark, this parasitic fungus is popularly called chaga — what's its scientific name?
Inonotus obliquus (a Latinization of the Russian word), is a fungus in the family Hymenochaetaceae.
Best known for his laws of planetary motion, this German astronomer has also been called the 'father of science fiction' for his novel Somnium. Who is he?
Johannes Kepler (27 December 1571 - 15 November 1630) was a German polymath who was an astronomer, mathematician, astrologer, natural philosopher and music theorist.

Normally part of the healthy flora in the mouth, skin, and gut, this rod-shaped bacterium can turn destructive if aspirated into the lungs, producing a telltale bloody, brick-colored jelly-like sputum — what's the organism?
Klebsiella pneumoniae is a Gram-negative, non-motile, encapsulated, lactose-fermenting, facultative anaerobic, rod-shaped bacterium.
Found in all land animals with internal skeletons, this fibrous band connects bones to other bones and, in birds and dinosaurs, secures flight feathers in place — what is it?
Ligament is a type of fibrous connective tissue in the body that connects bones to other bones.
Found in nearly every animal cell but rare in plants, this membrane-bound organelle acts as the cell's degradation center, breaking proteins, sugars, and fats into their building blocks — what is it?
Lysosome (/lassom/) is a membrane-bound organelle that is found in all animal cells (except red blood cells), and rarely in plant cells.

Designed as both fighter and ground-attack aircraft (hence the F/A designation), this all-weather supersonic, carrier-capable twin-engined jet was derived from the YF-17 and developed for the Navy. What aircraft is this?

McDonnell Douglas F/A-18 Hornet is an all-weather supersonic, twin-engined, carrier-capable, multirole combat aircraft, designed as both a fighter and ground attack aircraft (hence the F/A designation).

This synthetic prostaglandin drug can prevent stomach ulcers in people taking NSAIDs, induce labor, treat dangerous postpartum bleeding, and — alone or paired with another drug — end a pregnancy — what's the medication?

Misoprostol is a synthetic prostaglandin medication used to prevent and treat stomach and duodenal ulcers, induce labor, cause an abortion, and treat postpartum bleeding due to poor contraction of the uterus.

Native to the Horn of Africa and nicknamed the 'sand puppy,' this burrowing rodent is the only mammal that's a cold-blooded thermoconformer — and lives in an insect-like colony with a single breeding queen. What is it?
Naked mole-rat (Heterocephalus glaber), also known as the sand puppy, is a burrowing rodent native to the Horn of Africa and parts of Kenya, notably in Somali regions.
This basic mathematical object is used to count, measure, and label, most commonly represented today through the Hindu-Arabic system of ten symbols — what fundamental concept is it?
Number is a mathematical object used to count, measure, and label. The most basic examples are the natural numbers: 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, and so forth.
Jointly built by Italy, the UK and Germany, this variable-sweep-wing combat aircraft comes in strike, electronic-warfare and interceptor variants — which jet?
Panavia Tornado is a family of twin-engine, variable-sweep wing multi-role combat aircraft, jointly developed and manufactured by Italy, the United Kingdom and Germany.
Dubbed the "father of transplantation," this Brazilian-born biologist shared a 1960 Nobel Prize for his discovery of acquired immune tolerance. Who was he?

Peter Medawar (28 February 1915 - 2 October 1987) was a Brazilian-born biologist and writer of Lebanese-British descent who, from a succession of research and teaching posts (Oxford through the Royal Institution), and senior U.K.
Which silvery-white precious metal carries the symbol Pt, leads group 10 of the periodic table, and is far rarer in Earth's crust than its glittering cousins?
Platinum is a chemical element; it has symbol Pt and atomic number 78.
Classified into acute, chronic, and pelvic pain syndrome subtypes, this condition doesn't always match its name's literal meaning of organ swelling — which condition?
Prostatitis is an umbrella term for a variety of medical conditions that incorporate bacterial and non-bacterial origin illnesses in the pelvic region.

This bird of prey now breeds only in Europe, though it once also ranged across West Asia and Northwest Africa, with northern populations historically wintering as far as western Africa — what bird is it?
Red kite (Milvus milvus) is a bird of prey in the family Accipitridae, which also includes many other diurnal raptors such as eagles, buzzards, and harriers.
This root vegetable — a hybrid of cabbage and a related turnip-like plant — goes by different names in North America and Britain, and is often confused for a big turnip. What is it?
Rutabaga (North American English) or swede (British English and some Commonwealth English) is a root vegetable, a form of Brassica napus (which also includes rapeseed).

This potentially life-threatening condition occurs when the body's dysregulated response to infection damages its own tissues and organs, often causing fever, rapid heartbeat, and confusion — what is it called?
Sepsis is a potentially life-threatening condition that arises when the body's dysregulated response to infection causes injury to its own tissues and organs.
Called sun spiders, camel spiders, and wind scorpions, these dry-climate arachnids are neither true spiders nor scorpions, and urban legends wildly exaggerate their danger — what order are they?
Solifugae is an order of arachnids known variously as solifuges, sun spiders, camel spiders, wind scorpions, and jerrymanders.
Generated in mitochondria via the TCA cycle, this dicarboxylic compound gets converted into fumarate by an enzyme that helps build ATP — which molecule?
Succinic acid is a dicarboxylic acid with the chemical formula (CH2)2(CO2H)2.

Named for the order of fish that includes pufferfish, this potent neurotoxin also turns up in blue-ringed octopuses and rough-skinned newts, and is actually produced by symbiotic bacteria rather than the animals themselves — what's the toxin?

Tetrodotoxin (TTX) is a potent neurotoxin. Its name derives from Tetraodontiformes, an order that includes pufferfish, porcupinefish, ocean sunfish, and triggerfish; several of these species carry the toxin.

A phenylpiperazine compound in the serotonin antagonist and reuptake inhibitor class, this antidepressant treats depression, anxiety and insomnia but carries a rare risk of prolonged, painful erections — which drug?
Trazodone is an antidepressant medication used to treat major depressive disorder, anxiety disorders, and insomnia.
Once classified in the honeysuckle family before molecular studies gave it its own, this genus of 150-plus shrub species reaches Africa only via the Atlas Mountains — which genus?
Viburnum is a genus of about 150-175 species of flowering plants in the family Viburnaceae.

Extracted from birch wood and named for the Greek word for 'wood', this white crystalline sugar alcohol is more soluble in water than any other common sugar alcohol except sorbitol. Name the compound?
Xylitol is an organic compound with the formula HOCH(CH(OH)CH2OH)2.
Caused by a mutation in the FGFR3 gene, this genetic disorder is the most common cause of short stature, marked by shortened limbs, a normal-length torso and a prominent forehead — what is it called?
Achondroplasia: Genetic condition, the most common form of dwarfism.
With wingspans reaching up to eleven and a half feet, which large seabird family ranges across the Southern Ocean and North Pacific but is absent from the North Atlantic?
Albatross: Family of large seabirds. The albatrosses are usually regarded as falling into four genera, but disagreement exists over the number of species.
Also known as shadbush, serviceberry, or juneberry, this rose-family shrub's berries inspired the name of a Canadian city — which genus?
First described by a German entomologist in 1818 and known as the 'marsh mosquito,' this genus is the only one that transmits malaria to humans — which genus is it?
Anopheles: Genus of mosquito. The genus Anopheles diverged from other mosquitoes approximately 100 million years ago (mya), and, like other mosquitoes, the eggs, larvae, and pupae are aquatic.

Nicknamed for its resemblance to a stinging insect, this orb-weaver spider sports bold yellow, white, and black bands across Central and Northern Europe, parts of Asia and Africa, and even the Azores — what species is it?
Argiope bruennichi: Species of orb-weaver spider. Like many other members of the same genus Argiope, this species has distinctive yellow, white and black markings on its abdomen.
From the Greek for "self-devouring," this lysosome-driven process lets a cell tidily break down and recycle its own worn-out parts — what is it?
Autophagy: Process of cells digesting parts of themselves.

Nicknamed 'Huey,' this American utility helicopter became the first turbine-powered rotorcraft in U.S. military service, developed in the 1950s to meet an Army need for medical evacuation and utility missions. Which aircraft?
Bell UH-1 Iroquois: Huey family of American military utility helicopters.
This insect order unites cockroaches with termites, after genetic evidence showed termites are actually evolved, eusocial cockroaches. What's the order called?
Blattodea: Order of insects that includes cockroaches and termites.
Created in 1993 by Swiss student Urban Müller, this esoteric programming language uses just eight simple commands and is often cited as a 'Turing tarpit' — what is it called?
Brainfuck: Esoteric, minimalist programming language. While Brainfuck is fully Turing-complete, it is not intended for practical use but to challenge and amuse programmers.
Its Latin name means "chisel-bearing," a nod to the stout egg-laying organs of its members — which insect suborder includes grasshoppers, ground-hoppers, and pygmy mole crickets?
Caelifera: Suborder of insects. The latter should not be confused with the mole crickets (Gryllotalpidae), which belong to the other Orthopteran suborder Ensifera.
A founder of humanistic psychology, this American psychologist pioneered person-centered therapy, an approach that also shaped student-centered learning in education — who is he?
Certified in 1984 and developed into a freighter variant for FedEx, this single-engine turboprop utility plane typically seats nine and can be fitted with floats or skis — which aircraft?
Cessna 208 Caravan: Family of utility transport aircraft.
Blooming in autumn and closely associated with the month of November, this East Asian flowering genus in the daisy family boasts thousands of horticultural varieties — which flower?
Chrysanthemum: Genus of flowering plants in the daisy family.

Believed to be the first coffee species ever cultivated, this plant, native to the forests of Ethiopia, South Sudan, and Yemen, still accounts for roughly 60% of global coffee production — what's its scientific name?
Coffea arabica: Species of coffee plant. Coffea arabica, also known as the Arabica coffee, is a species of flowering plant in the coffee and madder family Rubiaceae.
Born in 1863, this Italian is remembered as a major contributor to the early development of algebraic geometry — who was he?
This herpesvirus genus's human species can cause mononucleosis in adults but birth defects affecting the eyes, ears, liver, and spleen when passed to a fetus — which virus?
Cytomegalovirus: Genus of viruses. The 11 species in this genus include Human cytomegalovirus (HCMV, HHV-5), which is the species that infects humans.
Marked by up to 20 liters of dilute urine a day and intense thirst that drinking barely satisfies, this condition comes in four types tied to problems with the hormone vasopressin — what is it?
Diabetes insipidus: Condition characterized by large amounts of dilute urine and increased thirst.
Working alongside biochemist Katalin Karikó on nucleoside base modifications, this University of Pennsylvania immunologist shared the 2023 Nobel Prize for enabling COVID-19 mRNA vaccines — who is he?
Drew Weissman: American physician and immunologist (born 1959)
First described in 1821, this family of large herbivorous mammals features a snout modified into a trunk and includes extinct relatives such as mammoths — which taxonomic family?
Elephantidae: Family of mammals. The family was first described by John Edward Gray in 1821, and later assigned to taxonomic ranks within the order Proboscidea.

Arising in the food pipe that runs between the throat and the stomach, this disease's two main subtypes are a squamous-cell form common in the developing world and a glandular form more common in developed nations. What is it?
Esophageal cancer: Malignant neoplastic disease of the esophagus.
Carried out by the lungs, kidneys, and skin in vertebrates, this bodily process rids the body of metabolic byproducts like urea, carbon dioxide, and uric acid — what is it called?
Excretion: Elimination of metabolic waste products by an organism.

Modern phylogenetics calls this a paraphyletic group covering nearly every vertebrate except the tetrapods — gill-bearing, limbless-of-digits, and usually cold-blooded. What aquatic animals are these?

In math, this concept assigns exactly one element of a codomain to each element of a domain, and was formalized via set theory by the end of the 19th century after originating as a way to describe how one varying quantity depends on another — what is it called?
Function (mathematics): Association of one output to each input.

The largest species of its kind in the world, this circumglobal sea creature was reclassified in 2017 after DNA testing showed it was more closely related to a different genus than to its smaller reef-dwelling cousin — what is it?
Giant oceanic manta ray: Species of cartilaginous fish.
Known as the black shag in New Zealand, this widespread seabird breeds across much of the Old World, Australasia, and the Atlantic coast of North America — which bird?

Recognizable by V-shaped nostrils and a layer of blubber that keeps it warm in Arctic and temperate coastal waters, this pinniped is the most widely distributed of its kind and can weigh up to 370 pounds — which species?
Harbor seal: Species of pinniped. Blubber under the seal's skin helps to maintain body temperature.
This seasonal state of drastically reduced metabolism, breathing, and heart rate lets animals conserve energy through winter months, with 'aestivation' as its summer counterpart — what is it called?
Hibernation: Physiological state of dormant inactivity in order to pass the winter season.
This poisonous gas or liquid with the formula HF dissolves in water to form a corrosive acid and serves as the chief industrial source of fluorine — what is it?
Traditionally drawn from the leaves of Indigofera plants and now mostly made synthetically, this blue compound is the color most associated with denim and blue jeans — what is it?
Indigo dye: Chemical compound, food additive and dye.
This American climatologist's 1988 Congressional testimony helped awaken the public to global warming, and he later turned activist — getting arrested more than once for the cause. Who is it?

Born John Chapman, this American pioneer nurseryman planted seed-grown apple trees across Pennsylvania, Ohio and beyond, becoming a folk hero in his own lifetime for his kindness and conservation. By what nickname do we know him?
A pastor's son and theoretical physicist, this man passed Manhattan Project secrets to the Soviets, served nine years in a British prison, then resumed his science career in East Germany. Who is he?
Klaus Fuchs: German-born British physicist and atomic spy (1911–1988)

Named from the Greek word for 'honey bee' because its flowers attract them, this citrus-scented herb in the mint family has been cultivated since at least the 16th century for tea and aromatic oils — what is it?

Three of this crustacean's five pairs of legs bear claws, with the first pair often dramatically oversized, and its burrow-dwelling relatives include the Norway variety known as langoustine - which creature?
Lobster: Family of clawed marine crustaceans.
With deeply forked tails and iridescent, tiger-like stripes on their backs, these pelagic fish migrate in huge schools to shallow coastal spawning grounds — what are they?
Mackerel: Pelagic fish. Mackerel is a common name applied to a number of different species of pelagic fish, mostly from the family Scombridae.
This American psychologist completed every requirement for a Harvard Ph.D. in 1895 but was denied the degree because of her gender — who was she?
Mary Whiton Calkins: American philosopher and psychologist. In 1903, Calkins was the twelfth in a listing of fifty psychologists with the most merit, chosen by her peers.

From a Greek word meaning 'change,' this term covers the enzyme-driven reactions that turn food into usable energy and building blocks while excreting waste — letting organisms grow and reproduce. What is it?
Metabolism: Set of chemical reactions in organisms.

Prized for their fur and related to weasels and otters, these semiaquatic carnivores have established wild populations in Britain and Denmark after farm escapes and animal-rights releases — what are they?
Mink: Mammal in the family Mustelidae.
Also known as green gram, this legume is a staple ingredient across East, Southeast, and South Asian cuisine in both savory and sweet dishes — what is it?
Discovered in 1898 alongside krypton and xenon, this noble gas gets its name from the Greek word for 'new' and glows bright red in electrical discharge — what element is it?
Neon: Chemical element with atomic number 10 (Ne)

Sometimes called "radiology done inside out," this medical specialty records radiation emitted from within the body and emphasizes function over anatomy — using scans like SPECT and PET. What's the field?
Nuclear medicine: Medical specialty. Nuclear medicine (nuclear radiology) is a medical specialty involving the application of radioactive substances in the diagnosis and treatment of disease.
With atomic number 76 and symbol Os, this bluish-white transition metal has the highest density of any stable element and was once prized for fountain-pen nib tips — what is it?
Osmium: Chemical element with atomic number 76 (Os). Osmium (from Ancient Greek ὀσμή (osmḗ) 'smell') is a chemical element; it has symbol Os and atomic number 76.

Native across Europe, Asia, and Africa, this medium-sized game bird's family ties are murkier than expected — genetically, some species lean toward pheasants, others toward junglefowl. What bird is it?
Partridge: Common name for a type of bird.
This Belgian-British microbiologist helped discover the Ebola virus in 1976, fought to contain its first recorded outbreak, then became a pioneering AIDS researcher — who is he?
Also called threadworm in the UK and seatworm elsewhere, this common intestinal roundworm spreads via the faecal-oral route and is especially prevalent among children — what parasite is it?
A purplish-black crystalline salt that dissolves into an intensely pink-to-purple solution, this strong oxidizer also appears on the WHO's List of Essential Medicines for wound care — what is it?
This Greco-Roman scholar authored the Almagest on astronomy and the Geography, a treatise on maps and geographic knowledge — who is he?

In this condition, tiny arteries spasm and starve the fingers of blood, classically turning them white, then blue, then a burning red as flow returns. It's named for the physician who first described it in 1862 — what is it?
Raynaud syndrome: Medical condition in which spasm of arteries causes episodes of reduced blood flow.
Winner of the 1905 Nobel Prize for his tuberculosis research, this German physician's 1876 discovery of the anthrax bacterium is considered the birth of modern bacteriology — who is he?
Robert Koch: German physician and bacteriologist (1843–1910)
Held together by electrostatic forces called ionic bonds, this type of chemical compound pairs positive and negative ions into a substance with zero net charge — what class of compound?
Salt (chemistry): Chemical compound involving ionic bonding.
As chief technology officer of a Turkish defense company, this pilot-engineer designed Turkey's first indigenous unmanned combat aerial vehicle and its first unmanned fighter jet. Who is he?
Selçuk Bayraktar: Turkish engineer and businessman. Selçuk Bayraktar (born 7 October 1979) is a Turkish pilot, engineer and businessman.
Housing the eyes, ears, nose, and brain, this bony structure at the head end of a vertebrate is built from cranial bones, facial bones, and tiny fused ossicles — what is it?
Skull: Bony structure that forms the head in vertebrates.
Acting as a blood filter and red-blood-cell recycling center, which vertebrate organ also stores a reserve of blood for use during hemorrhagic shock?
Spleen: Immune organ that filters blood.
Codenamed 'Flanker' by NATO, this Soviet twin-engine fighter entered service in 1985 as an air-superiority answer to the F-14 and F-15 — what is it?
Sukhoi Su-27: Soviet 4th generation fighter aircraft.

A major constituent of bile and widely distributed in mammalian tissues, this compound is usually called an amino acid even though its sulfonic acid group keeps it out of protein synthesis. What is it?
Taurine: Aminosulfonic acid. Taurine is a major constituent of bile and can be found in the large intestine.

Marked by platelet counts that fall too low — sometimes below 50,000 per microliter and requiring emergency care — this blood disorder is the most common coagulation problem in ICU patients — what is it called?
Thrombocytopenia: Abnormally low levels of platelets in the blood.

This anabolic steroid, derived from the nandrolone group, is used legally in livestock to boost muscle growth but also circulates illegally on the black market under a shortened nickname — what is it?
Trenbolone: Anabolic steroid. Trenbolone is an androgen and anabolic steroid (AAS) of the nandrolone group which itself was never marketed for human use.
Historically fermented and used in gunpowder production, leather tanning, and textile dyeing, this bodily fluid also helps plants grow when used as fertilizer — what is it?
Urine: Liquid by-product of animal metabolism.
Belonging to the same family as kangaroos but generally smaller, this Australian marsupial has also been introduced to New Zealand, Hawaii, and the UK — what is it?
Wallaby: Macropods of Australia and New Guinea.
With atomic number 54, this dense, colorless noble gas was the first to form a stable chemical compound, and now doubles as a general anesthetic and ion-thruster propellant — which element?
Xenon: Chemical element with atomic number 54 (Xe). It is a dense, colorless, odorless noble gas found in Earth's atmosphere in trace amounts.

The symbol for uranium is U. Uranium is a chemical element; it has symbol U and atomic number 92.

Robin Wright: Robin Gayle Wright (born April 8, 1966) is an American actress, producer and director.
